patients.summary: Retired math teacher with Parkinson disease and medically managed CAD who joins in 2019; achalasia (2021) and wild-type ATTR cardiac amyloidosis (2021-22) follow, then a 2024 CABG complicated by heparin-related bleeding, sternal wound dehiscence, mediastinitis and left phrenic nerve injury, and in 2026 Parkinson disease psychosis managed by tapering pramipexole.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
66M here to establish care, transferring from his prior primary care office. Wife with him and fills in dates.

PD: diagnosed early 2016 at age 62 after his wife noticed a tremor in his right hand and that he'd gone quiet-faced. Seen by an outside neurology group, about twice a year. On carbidopa/levodopa 25/100 TID and pramipexole ER 1.5 mg daily. Says the tremor is mostly a nuisance; buttons are slow. No falls, no freezing, no lightheadedness on standing that he notices.

CAD: had a nuclear stress test in 2016 at his old practice, ordered for vague exertional fatigue; told it was abnormal, cardiology recommended medical therapy, never had a cath. No chest pain since. Aspirin 81 and atorvastatin 20.

Lipids: on atorvastatin for years.

Hands: numb fingers both sides for a couple of years, both wrists released in early 2018; numbness gone.

Meds reconciled from bottles: carbidopa/levodopa 25/100 TID, pramipexole ER 1.5 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily. NKDA.
FHx: father MI at 63. Mother had Alzheimer's. One older brother, hypertension.
SHx: retired after decades teaching high school math. Married. Never smoked, doesn't drink.

Exam: well appearing. BP and HR as recorded. Mild resting tremor R hand, reduced facial expression, slightly soft voice. Gait a bit slow, steady, turns in three steps. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. No edema. Healed volar wrist scars bilaterally.

A/P
1. Parkinson disease: stable on current regimen; continue with outside neurology. Will request their last note.
2. CAD, medically managed: asymptomatic. Continue aspirin, statin.
3. Hyperlipidemia: lipid panel today.
4. Health maintenance: prior records requested for colonoscopy and vaccine dates. High-dose flu today. HCV and HIV screening today, he agreed.
CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH drawn. Return 3 months.

documents.title: Prior primary care records
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
82 pages received by fax from previous primary care office, scanned. Pertinent items abstracted by RN:
- 05/2016 pharmacologic nuclear stress test: reported abnormal, read as consistent with coronary artery disease; cardiology letter recommends aspirin and statin, no catheterization at this time.
- 03/2016 neurology letter: Parkinson disease, carbidopa/levodopa started; pramipexole added later that year.
- 01/2018 and 03/2018 hand surgery op notes: right then left carpal tunnel release, uncomplicated.
- 06/2017 colonoscopy: normal to cecum, no polyps; repeat in 10 years.
- Vaccines: Tdap 5/2014, PCV13 10/2016, PPSV23 10/2017; yearly flu.
- No allergies listed.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Ronald, your blood work from the 17th came back fine. Blood counts, kidney and liver tests, and thyroid are normal. Hepatitis C and HIV screens negative. Cholesterol about where I'd expect on atorvastatin 20; we'll keep the same dose and recheck yearly. I also got your old office's records, including the 2017 colonoscopy, so you're set there for a while.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up after establishing. Saw neurology in November, no changes; they'll send a note. Walks the dog most mornings, about 20 min. No chest pain or pressure with walking or shoveling. Bowels a little slow, managing with prunes.
Exam: rest tremor R hand unchanged, mild hypomimia. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. No edema.
A/P: PD stable, CAD without angina, lipids on statin. No changes. Medicare wellness visit in the spring.

documents.title: Visit cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: In-person wellness visits paused this month. Called pt, offered video visit instead. Rebooked 4/21 by video.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from home, wife beside him, both doing fine and staying in. He's doing a math puzzle a day and walking the loop of their road. No chest symptoms. Tremor the same. Neurology appointment moved to video too.
Meds unchanged, 90-day supplies at mail order.
Plan: full wellness visit and labs in the fall when we can see him in person.

documents.title: Atorvastatin refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Mail-order pharmacy request for atorvastatin 20 mg #90 with 3 refills. Last lipids 9/2019. Approved per protocol.

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, masked visit. Wife present.
Function: independent in dressing, bathing, meals, finances; still drives locally in daylight. No falls in the past year. Timed up and go 11 s. Hearing and vision fine with readers.
Cognition: Mini-Cog 5/5.
Mood: PHQ-2 0.
Advance directive: wife is health care proxy, form on file now.
Exam: hypomimia, R hand rest tremor, mild cogwheeling R wrist. Heart regular. Lungs clear. No edema.
Prevention: colonoscopy 2017 normal. Flu high-dose and first Shingrix today; second dose in 2 months. Pneumococcal complete.
Plan: labs today. Continue meds. See in 6 months.

documents.title: Shingrix #2
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Second recombinant zoster dose given IM left deltoid. Said the first one made him tired for a day. Observed 15 min, fine. Series complete.
